business.description: IntraSoft Technologies is a technology-driven, multi-channel online retailer serving the U.S. market. The company acts as an e-commerce partner to small and medium-sized vendors, helping bridge the gap between product-focused brands and customer-focused marketplaces through its proprietary e-commerce platform and operating capabilities.

products.name: E-commerce marketplace operations and fulfilment services
products.note: Enables products to be listed, marketed, sold and fulfilled across leading online marketplaces; includes vendor onboarding, SKU selection, pricing, demand forecasting, inventory planning and fulfilment

plants.capacity: The Company is not engaged in the manufacturing activities and hence does not have any Plant.

outlook.statement: The U.S. e-commerce market continues to offer substantial long-term opportunity. The company will remain focused on disciplined execution, strengthening vendor relationships, expanding relevant product selection and improving the efficiency of its platform and processes.
OECD projects U.S. GDP growth of 2.0% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027. Global retail e-commerce sales estimated at $6.88 trillion in 2026 (7.2% YoY growth) and projected to approach $7.89 trillion by 2028.
A detailed review of the operations, performance and future outlook of the Company and its business is given in the Management's Discussion and Analysis Report and the same forms part of this Report.

risks: Technology, cybersecurity and platform change: Rapid technology change, data-security threats or marketplace-system changes could affect efficiency and service levels
Marketplace and policy concentration: Changes in marketplace policies, fees, algorithms or account requirements can affect sales and operating processes
Supply chain, tariffs and seasonal execution: Tariffs, carrier disruption, supplier constraints or peak-season demand can affect cost, availability and fulfilment
Key business risks and their mitigation are considered in the annual / strategic business plans and in periodic management reviews.
Credit risk from trade receivables and financial assets
Liquidity risk from maturity mismatches of financial assets and liabilities
Market risk from foreign exchange rate fluctuations (USD/INR)
Interest rate risk on variable rate borrowings

Foreign exchange risk arising from foreign currency transactions (IT enabled services), primarily with respect to the US Dollar

key_audit_matters: Recoverability of Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) Credit: As at March 31, 2026, the Parent Company has recognised Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) credit amounting to ₹1,529.46 Lacs, within deferred tax assets. The recognition of a deferred tax asset in the form of MAT credit is based on management's estimate of taxable and accounting profits in future, which are underpinned by the Company's price assumptions and business plans, and tax adjustments required to be made in the taxable profit computations, as per the provisions of Income-tax Act, 1961 (IT Act). Estimating recoverability of MAT credit also requires significant judgements, including the timing of reversals of unabsorbed business losses and depreciation.
Recoverability of Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) Credit: As at 31 March 2026, the Company has recognised Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) credit amounting to Rs.1529.46 Lacs, within deferred tax assets.
qualifications_or_emphasis: We did not audit the financial statements / financial information of one step down subsidiary whose financial statements reflect total assets of Rs. 102.85 Lakhs and net assets of Rs. 98.93 Lakhs as at March 31, 2026... which have been audited and furnished to us by their Independent auditors. Our opinion on the consolidated financial results, in so far as it related to the amounts and disclosures included in respect of these subsidiaries is based solely on the reports of other auditors and procedures performed by us as stated under Auditor's Responsibilities section above.

The financial statements of two subsidiaries and one step down subsidiary located outside India, included in the consolidated financial statements, which constitute total assets of Rs. 43518.90 Lakhs and net assets of Rs. 38723.66 Lakhs as at March 31, 2026... have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in its country. The Parent Company's management has converted the financial statements of such subsidiary located outside India from the accounting principles generally accepted in their respective countries to the accounting principles generally accepted in India. We have audited these conversion adjustments made by the Parent Company's management. Our opinion in so far as it relates to the balances and affairs of such subsidiaries located outside India, including other information, is based on the report of other auditor and the conversion adjustments prepared by the management of the Parent Company.
